Expert systems

Expert knowledge becomes explicit rules

Early MYCIN research explored rule-based advice in a tightly defined specialist domain.

Edward H. Shortliffe and colleagues

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

Expert systemsSymbolic AIReasoningKnowledge representation

The contribution

This paper describes an AI program for advising on antimicrobial therapy. It is a representative publication from expert-system research, where specialized knowledge and inference procedures were encoded explicitly to support decisions within a defined domain.

What this does not establish

A historical research system is not evidence of suitability for present-day clinical decisions. The entry makes no claim of routine clinical deployment.

Why this date?

The linked article appeared in December 1973; later MYCIN theses and reports have different dates.

This entry follows the linked publication. Read the source and date conventions.
